info.name: Royal Touche — Admin Panel
info.description:
Every endpoint the web panel calls, grouped the way the panel is.

Set `base_url`, `email` and `password`, then run **Auth → Login** — the token is stored and reused by every other request through collection-level bearer auth.

── Who can call what ──
  admin              everything
  godown_supervisor  master data + rolls/barcodes only; the panel hides the rest
  staff              GRN only
  store_manager /
  godown_operator    app-only accounts — the web login refuses them

── Conventions ──
  • every list of master data is unpaginated (pickers read it whole); documents, GRNs, vouchers, rolls and movements are paginated with page/pageSize
  • DELETE on master data is a SOFT delete — status goes to inactive, and PATCH status back to 'active' restores it
  • ids in `{{curly}}` are collection variables; fill them from a list response

The mobile app has its own collection: royal-touche-mobile.postman_collection.json. Do not use this one to test the phone — it does not carry the offline rules.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Login, token refresh, identity, and the invite / password-reset flows.

request.description:
Stores accessToken, refreshToken and role as collection variables. Every other request reuses the token through the collection's bearer auth.

The panel signs in with an admin or godown_supervisor account.
Swap a refresh token for a new access token. A 401 anywhere else means call this, then retry the original request once.
The signed-in user: id, name, email, role.
Revokes the refresh token. The access token stays valid until it expires.

The token comes from the invite email's link. Sets the password and signs the user in — except for app-only roles (store_manager, godown_operator), where the password is set but no web session starts.
Always answers the same way whether or not the address exists — it must not reveal who has an account.
Token from the reset email.

item.name: Master data
item.description:
Vendors (with their paper codes), godown locations, raw materials and remarks.

All four behave identically: read is open to any signed-in user (pickers need it), writes need admin / store_manager / godown_supervisor / godown_operator, and DELETE is a soft delete that sets status to inactive.

request.description: The whole vendors master — no pagination, it is read into a picker.
One vendor, with its embedded paper codes.
vendor_code is uppercased and must be unique. `papers` is the Royal Touche paper-codes sheet for this supplier — each row needs a royal_touche_code or a delta_code.

A PATCH carrying `papers` REPLACES the whole array — the sheet is edited as a set and the rows have no id to merge on. Omit `papers` to leave it untouched.

`contact` is the exception: it merges field by field.
Soft delete — sets status to inactive. Purchase history keeps pointing at it. PATCH status back to 'active' to restore.
The whole locations master — no pagination, it is read into a picker.
sort_order drives picker order — bays are walked in physical order, not alphabetical.
The whole raw materials master — no pagination, it is read into a picker.
The whole remarks master — no pagination, it is read into a picker.
Fills the picker behind `remark_code` on a roll and on a stock movement. The free-text `remarks` field stays available alongside it.
Soft delete. Rows that already recorded this code keep their meaning.

item.name: Rolls & stock (read)
item.description: Read-only in the panel. Rolls are registered and moved from the phone.

query.description: Roll number, RT code or batch

request.description: Paginated. This is what the barcode generator lists to pick rolls from.
One roll, with signed URLs for its four registration photos.
Label details only. `remaining_weight` and `status` are REFUSED here — stock moves through the ledger, never by editing the roll.
Removes a roll registered in error. Its ledger rows are what stock is derived from, so reach for a correcting ADJUSTMENT movement first — delete only a roll that should never have existed.

The append-only ledger. `description` is server-rendered — show it, don't rebuild it.

CONSUME rows come from the phone's 'roll finished' flag: used_weight is what was left on the roll, and roll_weight_after is 0.

request.description: Derived from the ledger, not stored by hand.

Step 3, after every PUT succeeded. Creates the documents and starts extraction.
Bytes relayed through this server. Kept until direct-to-GCS is proven in production.

item.name: Public GRN (no auth)
item.description: Deliberately public — mounted before the authenticated catch-all so no token is required. Anyone with the URL can read and decide these GRNs; keep that in mind before pointing it at anything sensitive.
